Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000548": The billing API is owned by the Atlas team as of 2025-06-09, having moved from the Ember team; the Boreal team was recorded by mistake and never held it.  (about: Atlas team, Boreal team, billing API, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000497": As of 2025-06-24, the reporting service still relies on the ledger service.  (about: ledger service, reporting service)
- memory_id "1000488": Tomasz is on the Atlas team on-call rotation as of 2025-06-19, taking over from Priya Raman.  (about: Atlas team, Priya Raman, Tomasz)
- memory_id "1000482" [constraint]: Tomasz holds the Atlas pager this cycle as of 2025-06-19; page Tomasz for anything Atlas-related, not Priya Raman.  (about: Atlas team, Priya Raman, Tomasz)
- memory_id "1000442" [decision]: Ledger migrations will ship with a reviewed query plan.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000424" [decision]: The indexer is owned by the Atlas team as of 2025-05-20, taking over from Cinder.  (about: Atlas team, Cinder, indexer)
- memory_id "1000387": On 2025-05-07 the Boreal team pinged the owners of the authentication gateway about the error rate.  (about: Boreal team, authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000368": As of 2025-04-29, the job scheduler still relies on the feature-flags service.  (about: feature-flags, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000286": On 2025-03-26 the Dune team observed that the notification service's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Dune team, notification service)
- memory_id "1000253": The ledger service relies on the auth gateway for service tokens, so if the auth gateway is down, the ledger service is down.  (about: ledger service, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000230": On 2025-02-21 the Boreal team pinged the owners of the ledger service about the memory growth.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000227": On 2025-02-21 the Boreal team noticed that the ledger service's memory use had grown steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000169": The root cause of INC-2025-004 was a consumer offset stuck after a broker restart.  (about: INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000160" [constraint]: The ledger service must stay on Postgres 14 until the partitioning work finishes.  (about: ledger service, Postgres 14)
- memory_id "1000109" [constraint]: The ledger service only ships on weekday mornings before 11:00 UTC.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000089": The billing API depends on the ledger service for invoice postings.  (about: ledger service, billing API)
- memory_id "1000075": Tomasz has the first on-call rotation for the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, Tomasz)
- memory_id "1000043": The feature-flags service is owned by the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, feature-flags)
- memory_id "1000033": The ledger service is owned by the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000001": The Atlas team in 2025 consists of Priya Raman and Tomasz.  (about: Atlas team, Priya Raman, Tomasz)

Actually, re-reading: "When the note changes something an existing fact states, do not add a contradicting fact." Reaffirmation isn't a change. Given the schema's purpose (graph memory upkeep), I'll add the fact as a confirmation with the date, entities: Atlas team, ledger service. Evidence: "The ledger remains a Atlas service."

Alternatively, empty. Hmm. The test likely wants empty arrays since nothing new. But there is a durable statement. I'll go with adding the confirmation fact — it records that ownership was reconfirmed on 2025-07-17, which is durable and useful (e.g., for staleness tracking).
